clue.text: Sex position daughters came to see

parts.note: sex is Latin for six, written as the Roman numeral VI
a site is a position or location
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter(s)

explanation.surface: A racy line about a sexual position that daughters wandered in to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex' is not about intimacy at all: it is the Latin word for six, so it becomes the Roman numeral VI.
explanation.definitionFit: To have visited someone is to have gone along and paid them a call in person.

clue.text: Climber untested: a recipe for disaster on Eiger's flanks

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things wrecked and jumbled, so the letters come out in a ruined order

parts.note: virgin means untried, never yet used or tested
these seven letters are rearranged

indicators.note: the flanks of something are its two sides, so only the edge letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the mountain's name

explanation.surface: A mountaineer with no experience attempting the Eiger is heading for catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, which the Eiger reinforces, but the climber is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia creeper is a vigorous vine that clambers up walls and fences, so it is a climbing plant.

clue.text: Initial jobs for travel guides

parts.note: to initial a document is to sign it
posts are jobs or positions of employment

explanation.surface: Someone's first employment was as a tour guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initial' reads as an adjective meaning first, but here it is the verb: putting your initials on something.
explanation.definitionFit: Signposts stand at roadsides pointing the way, so they direct people on a journey.

clue.text: See torn-up root in odd places

indicators.note: the odd places are positions one, three, five and so on, so only those letters are taken

parts.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: An uprooted plant's root lying around in unusual spots.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is the area or seat of a bishop; Truro, in Cornwall in south-west England, is a cathedral city. 'Torn-up' looks like an anagram signal but is only part of the source text.
explanation.definitionFit: Truro is the seat of a Church of England diocese, and a bishop's seat is called a see.

clue.text: Enduring blues performance, crowd confined

indicators.note: something confined is shut inside something else, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: a deed is an act, a performance of something
a press is a crowd or throng of people

explanation.surface: A long-lasting blues gig where the audience is packed in tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blues performance' looks like a musical phrase, but the definition ends at 'blues', which means low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone suffering the blues is sad and low, which is exactly what being depressed means.

clue.text: British trains losing time in seaside places

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for British

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: to train someone is to teach them
T is the abbreviation for time; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: British railway services running late on the way to coastal resorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trains' looks like railway carriages, but it is the verb meaning instructs.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaches are the sandy or pebbly shores where people go on holiday by the sea.

clue.text: Drink, black, to leak out slowly

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to ooze is to seep out gradually

explanation.surface: A dark drink seeping slowly from a container.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas make it look like a list describing a drink; in fact 'Drink' is the definition and the rest builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Booze is the informal word for alcoholic drink, used as both noun and verb.

clue.text: Ace forward, certain to delay header, finds gaps

indicators.note: delaying the header means the leading letter arrives later, moving from the front to the back

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace, as on playing cards
forward in the sense of cheeky or bold
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A star footballer, sure to hold back on heading the ball, keeps finding space.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture of an ace forward and a header is a disguise: 'forward' means saucy, and the 'header' is the first letter of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Apertures are openings or holes, so they are gaps in something.

clue.text: Dog with a sore throat?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sled dog of the Arctic

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a riddle about a poorly dog, but the two halves are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a breed of sled dog and also describes a hoarse, croaky voice.

clue.text: Needing bread with ingredients taken up, a chef drops bananas

indicators.note: in a down entry, taking something up lifts it upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: ingredients are the parts of a recipe

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

parts.note: these ten letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook short of a loaf drops the bananas while gathering ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money, and 'bananas' looks like another food item but signals crazy rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapped for cash is an idiom for short of money, and bread is old slang for money.

clue.text: Distinguished academic: one in four progresses improperly

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one letter joins the middle of the others
done improperly means done wrongly, so the letters end up in an incorrect order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be mixed
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A complaint that a quarter of senior scholars rise through the ranks by dubious means.
explanation.walkthrough: A Regius professor holds a chair founded by the Crown at an old British university such as Oxford, Cambridge or a Scottish one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Regius chair is a royally created professorship, among the most prestigious posts a scholar can hold.

clue.text: Tees is for ambassador abandoning urgent upgrade

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so those letters drop out

parts.note: Tees is the setter, so from the setter's mouth this is I'M
pro means in favour of
vehement means forceful and insistent
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: The setter Tees declares support for an envoy quitting a pressing promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Tees is the setter of this puzzle, so 'Tees is' stands for I'M. An ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated HE.
explanation.definitionFit: An upgrade makes something better, and a change for the better is an improvement.

clue.text: Old man needing year to travel west in bark

indicators.note: in an across entry, west is leftward, so travelling west means reading right to left

parts.note: one's old man is one's father, PA
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A father who needs a year to sail westward on a barque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bark' suggests a sailing ship, matching the travel picture, but it is the dog's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A yap is the short shrill cry of a small dog, a kind of bark.

clue.text: An extra page a day for teachers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a leaf or section inserted into a publication
second meaning: the British acronym for In-Service Education and Training

explanation.walkthrough: In British schools an INSET day is a staff training day when pupils stay at home.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a sheet slipped into a book or magazine, and is also the name of a teacher training day.

clue.text: These we may require, or one as pot's boiled

indicators.note: boiling churns and tumbles everything about, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be mixed

explanation.surface: Kitchen talk about what we will need while the kettle comes to the boil.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: making tea once the pot has boiled, we may need these to stir or measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Teaspoons are what a tea-maker reaches for when the brew is ready, so they are what we may need.

clue.text: Doctor Spooner's French cheese grab

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds trade places

parts.note: a soft, creamy cheese from the region near Paris
to seize is to grab hold of; the opening sounds of the two words then swap

explanation.surface: A physician named Spooner snatching some French cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a title attached to Spooner, but it is the definition: in hot places such as Perth or the Caribbean a cooling afternoon sea wind is called the Doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: In warm coastal regions the refreshing onshore wind is nicknamed the Doctor for its relief from heat.

clue.text: Advanced paper turns up containing a device that's similar

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so one piece goes within another
in a down entry, turning up flips the word upward, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: The Sun is a British newspaper
a plus logo, a device being an emblem or badge

explanation.surface: A progressive newspaper appears carrying a gadget that resembles something.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper. A device in heraldry or branding is an emblem, so a logo.
explanation.definitionFit: Analogous describes things that correspond or are comparable in some respect, so alike.

clue.text: River keeps running at speed, being clear

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold onto it, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
a machine that is running is on
rate is speed, as in going at a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A river flowing fast with clear water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' looks like an adjective about the water, but it is the verb: to clear someone of blame.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to declare a person free of guilt, absolving them of an accusation.

clue.text: Treated as canards — her prophecies were!

definitions.text: Treated as canards — her prophecies were!

indicators.note: treating something processes and alters it, so the letters are worked into another order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be mixed

explanation.surface: A lament for a prophet whose true warnings were dismissed as hoaxes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the mixed letters spell her name, and the full sentence describes her fate.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the Trojan princess was cursed to foretell truly but never be believed, her warnings dismissed as lies.

clue.text: Thus female crosses river in satirical piece

indicators.note: something that crosses another lies over and around it, so one piece straddles the other

parts.note: so means thus
the Po is the longest river in Italy
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman wading across a river in a comic sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: The female comes last in the answer even though she is named before the river, because only the first word wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoof is a humorous imitation that mocks its target, which is what a satirical piece does.

clue.text: Muse has to leave for day

indicators.note: whatever has to leave goes away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Erato is the Greek Muse of love poetry
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: An inspiring Muse must depart for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like part of 'has to leave' but it is the letters that do the leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Day in the sense of 'in my day' means a period of time, which is what an era is.

clue.text: American on journey no longer anchored

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: A US traveller whose ship has weighed anchor.
explanation.walkthrough: Atrip is a nautical term: an anchor is atrip when it has just been lifted clear of the sea bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors say an anchor is atrip once it is broken out of the ground, so it no longer holds the ship.

clue.text: Silly to cover up when protecting a right stirrer

indicators.note: to protect something is to shield it on all sides, so one piece wraps round another
silly means foolish and disordered, so the letters are thrown into a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be mixed
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: It is foolish to hide things while shielding a right-wing agitator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' could be a cricket fielding position, but here it signals the rearrangement of all the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrer is someone who deliberately causes trouble, which is what a provocateur does to incite reaction.

clue.text: Love shown by wise man in Siouan language

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A wise elder expresses affection in a Native American tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Osage is the language of the Osage Nation of the American Midwest, part of the Siouan family.
explanation.definitionFit: The Osage people of Missouri and Oklahoma speak a tongue belonging to the Siouan family of Native American languages.

clue.text: Old car in failing to start brings hot displeasure

indicators.note: failing to start means missing the beginning, so the first letter goes

parts.note: banger is British slang for an old, battered car; its first letter is removed

explanation.surface: A clapped-out car that will not start makes its owner furious.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a banger is a worn-out old car.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger is a strong feeling of annoyance, and heated irritation is a fair description of it.

clue.text: One to ignore grandma has struck arrogant pose outside

indicators.note: something struck is knocked about, so the letters are battered into a new order
one piece sitting outside another surrounds it, wrapping round it

parts.note: these twelve letters are rearranged
nan is a British word for grandmother

explanation.surface: Granny has adopted a haughty attitude towards someone she means to snub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has struck' reads as a verb phrase for granny, but 'struck' alone signals the rearrangement and 'has' just joins. Nan is a common British word for grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: Persona non grata is a Latin phrase for an unwelcome person, someone officially shunned.

clue.text: Sharp answer in Tripos test

indicators.note: being in something means lying inside it, so the letters sit within the following words

parts.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A smart reply given in a Cambridge exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tripos is the honours degree examination at Cambridge University.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, cutting retort, originally a fencing term for a swift counter-thrust.

clue.text: Terrifying sound rocks church

parts.note: scree is loose broken rock on a mountain slope
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A dreadful noise shakes a church to its foundations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' looks like a verb meaning shakes, but it is a noun for loose stones.
explanation.definitionFit: A screech is a harsh, piercing cry of the kind that can frighten anyone hearing it.
